description: The line plot illustrates the number of shared Top-6 routed experts between two independent samples for six different task domains—Intent, Summary, Law, Translation, Code, and Math—as a function of sample token count, which ranges from 2⁹ to 2²⁰ on a logarithmic x-axis. The y-axis, labeled “Shared Experts for Two Samples,” quantifies the average number of shared experts per model layer, spanning from 2.0 to 6.0. The “Intent” task (orange line) begins near 3.8 at 2⁹ tokens, dips slightly to ~3.9 at 2¹¹, then rises steadily to ~5.9 at 2²⁰. The “Summary” task (blue line) starts at 2.0, climbs sharply to ~4.8 at 2¹², dips to ~4.5 at 2¹⁴, then rises to ~5.9 by 2²⁰. The “Law” task (yellow line) begins at ~3.6, peaks at ~5.1 at 2¹¹, dips to ~4.6 at 2¹², then climbs to ~5.9 at 2²⁰. The “Translation” task (purple line) starts at ~5.1, peaks at ~5.6 at 2¹³, dips slightly to ~5.5 at 2¹⁴, then stabilizes near 5.9. The “Code” task (gray line) begins at 2.0, rises to ~3.0 at 2¹¹, peaks at ~3.8 at 2¹³, dips to ~3.1 at 2¹⁴, then climbs to ~5.8 at 2²⁰. The “Math” task (green line) starts at ~3.8, rises steadily to ~5.9 at 2²⁰, with a slight dip around 2¹⁴. All tasks converge near 5.9–6.0 experts shared at the largest sample size (2²⁰ tokens), indicating high consistency in expert routing at scale.
